name: Firecut
tagline: AI plugin that cuts silences, filler words and bad takes inside Premiere Pro and Resolve.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The underlying trick is not exotic: transcribe with Whisper, find silences and filler words, emit a cut list. An agent can build a CLI that ingests your footage and spits out an EDL or FCP7 XML you drop into Premiere or Resolve, and for a talking head podcast that covers most of the value. What it cannot one-shot is living inside the NLE: a panel that reads your actual sequence, respects your existing edits, handles multicam and multitrack audio, and lets you undo one cut instead of reimporting a timeline. Accuracy on "bad take" and filler detection is also a tuning problem, not a coding problem, and you will spend the weekend on thresholds. Good build if your edits are simple, annoying build if your projects are real.
coreLoopDIY: Transcribes your footage locally, detects silence, filler words and repeated takes, and writes a timeline file your NLE can import.
requirements: a Whisper model download (a few GB, GPU strongly preferred)
an NLE that imports FCP7 XML or EDL
patience for threshold tuning on your own footage
whatYouLose: An in-app panel: no reading your live sequence, no incremental re-cut, no native undo
Multicam and multitrack audio handling, which is where most real projects live
Tuned filler word and repeated take detection that does not eat your breaths and beats
Someone else eating the maintenance when Adobe changes its extension API
Speed on long footage if you do not have a GPU
moatNotes: The moat is the plugin surface, not the model. Talking to Premiere's project state without corrupting it is the part nobody wants to write twice.
whyPeopleStillPay: Editors pay to stay in the app. A CLI that hands you an XML means an export, an import, a relink and a lost undo history, and that friction is exactly the friction the product exists to delete. Add multicam, mixed frame rates, and the fact that professional time is billable, and a subscription is cheaper than a weekend of threshold tuning plus a permanent round-trip tax on every project.
notes: The cut list is a weekend; the panel inside Premiere is the product.
prompt:
Build a local command line tool called roughcut that produces a silence-and-filler-trimmed timeline from raw video, for import into Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, single package, uv for deps, Typer for the CLI
- ffmpeg and ffprobe invoked as subprocesses
- faster-whisper for transcription with word level timestamps
- OpenTimelineIO for writing FCP7 XML and EDL output
- pytest for tests, no web UI, no server, no accounts, no telemetry

Commands:
- roughcut transcribe INPUT: extract mono 16k wav, run faster-whisper (model name from .env, default large-v3), cache the word level transcript as JSON next to the input keyed by file hash
- roughcut plan INPUT: from the cached transcript plus ffmpeg silencedetect, build a keep-list of segments and write plan.json with every decision and a reason string per removed span
- roughcut export INPUT: write roughcut.fcpxml (FCP7 XML flavor via OpenTimelineIO) and roughcut.edl referencing the original media, plus an optional --render flag that concatenates keeps into a preview mp4 via ffmpeg concat demuxer
- roughcut review INPUT: print a human readable table of removed spans with timecodes and reasons

Detection rules, all tunable via flags with sane defaults:
- silence: dBFS threshold and minimum duration, with configurable lead-in and tail padding so cuts do not clip consonants
- filler words: match a configurable word list (um, uh, like, you know, so yeah) using transcript word timestamps, only remove when the word is bounded by pauses
- repeated takes: detect near-duplicate consecutive sentences by normalized token similarity and keep the last one
- never produce a cut shorter than a configurable minimum, snap all cut points to frame boundaries using the probed frame rate

Explicitly out of scope: multicam, multitrack audio, speaker diarization, an Adobe or Resolve panel, GUI, cloud anything.

Deliverables: README with a one paragraph quickstart and a real example command, .env.example with WHISPER_MODEL and WHISPER_DEVICE, tests covering frame snapping, padding math and EDL timecode formatting using synthetic fixtures. Fail loudly with a clear message if ffmpeg is missing.
